summary: The root صلي (Sly) primarily means to be exposed to fire or heat, to roast, or to burn.

headwords.def: اصطلى He warmed himself (M, K) بِالنَّارِ [ by means of the fire ]: (M:) one says, اِصْطَلَيْتُ بِالنَّارِ and بِهَا [app. meaning I warmed myself by means of the fire ]: (S:) or اصطلى النَّارَ and بِالنَّارِ mean he became warm by means of the fire: and بِالنَّارِ , he became burnt by the fire. (MA.) Hence, in the Kur [xxvii. 7 and xxviii. 29], لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ [ May-be ye will warm yourselves ]: (TA:) in relation to which it is said that the time was winter, and therefore الاِصْطِلَآء was needed. (M, TA.) It is also said of the chameleon, as meaning He repaired to the sun. (M and L in art. شقذ : see an ex. in a verse cited voce شَقَذَانٌ .) And one says of a courageous man, with whom one cannot cope, لَا يُصْطَلَى بِنَارِهِ

headwords.def: مُصْطَلًى The limbs of a man, or his arms and legs and face and every prominent part, which become cold at the time of death, and which are warmed at the fire: (AHeyth, L in art. برد :) or the face and extremities.
